close_reason: Added UTCOffset newtype (RFC 5545 / RFC 8984 §4.7.2 TZOFFSETFROM/TZOFFSETTO format) consistent with LocalDateTime, Duration, SignedDuration newtype shape: #[non_exhaustive] tuple-struct around String with From<String>/From<&str>/AsRef<str>/Display impls, no validation (parsing deferred to backend per PLAN.md). Switched TimeZoneRule.offset_from and offset_to to UTCOffset. Breaking change to field type but acceptable: crate is pre-1.0 and structs are #[non_exhaustive]. Updated downstream tests in jmap-calendars-types and jmap-tasks-types (the only consumers that compared offsets directly to &str — they now call .as_ref()). cargo test --workspace + cargo clippy --workspace -D warnings clean.
description:
src/lib.rs:665, 669 type TimeZoneRule.offset_from and offset_to as bare String fields. RFC 8984 §4.7.2 specifies these as 'TZOFFSETFROM property from iCalendar' / 'TZOFFSETTO property from iCalendar' — iCalendar (RFC 5545 §3.3.14) defines the value as a signed UTC offset in the format ±HHMM or ±HHMMSS.

The crate already has three other 'spec-defined string format' newtypes (LocalDateTime, Duration, SignedDuration) modeled as transparent newtypes to document intent at the type level without validating. The offset strings follow exactly the same precedent — a well-defined ABNF shape with no parsing — yet they remain bare String.

Two consequences:

1. A consumer reading offset_from has no type-level signal that this is a signed offset (vs. an arbitrary tz id, a localized name, etc.). Compare to TimeZone.tz_id which is also a bare String — but there the spec says tzId is 'a valid paramtext value' which is much less specific than '±HHMM[SS]'.

2. The crate's documented design pattern (PLAN.md §70-82: 'These wrappers exist to document intent at the type level') applied unevenly. A future contributor adding a new typed temporal field will reasonably ask why offset_from is not a newtype while LocalDateTime is.

Two options:

(a) Add an UtcOffset newtype with the same minimal impl set as the other three newtypes, and use it for offset_from and offset_to.

(b) Document the deliberate choice to leave offset strings as String — perhaps because the format is iCalendar-derived rather than RFC-8984-native, or because no consumer is expected to programmatically inspect the value.

Recommendation: (a) — the precedent is established, the consumer surface is small (only TimeZoneRule), the change is non-breaking (#[non_exhaustive]). This is a P3 polish item, not load-bearing.
title: TimeZoneRule.offset_from / offset_to: String without typed shape, no validation, no Display divergence from Duration newtypes
